Four-panel illustration showing overhead views of different cropping systems. Panel 1 (Monocropping): A field uniformly filled with parallel rows of maize plants. Panel 2 (Mixed cropping): A scattered, random mix of yam mounds, cassava, and maize plants with no clear rows. Panel 3 (Intercropping): Neat, alternating rows of tall maize and low-lying groundnut. Panel 4 (Strip cropping): Broad alternating bands of crops curving along a hillside slope; one band is tall maize, the next is dense green cowpea.

Three-panel diagram illustrating planting patterns. Panel 1 (Broadcasting): A farmer's hand scattering small seeds randomly over a patch of flat soil, with arrows showing seeds falling everywhere. Panel 2 (Row spacing): A top-down view of seeds placed at exact, equal intervals (e.g., 50 cm apart) along straight, measured lines, forming a grid. Panel 3 (Drilling): A tractor-drawn seed drill cutting shallow furrows, dropping seeds continuously into the lines, and covering them with soil.

Three side-by-side panels showing the effect of plant density on maize. Panel 1 (Low Density): A few large, robust maize plants spaced very far apart, with weeds growing in the wide gaps between them. Panel 2 (Optimum Density): Healthy, strong maize plants with large cobs, spaced perfectly to cover the soil without crowding each other. Panel 3 (High Density): Very crowded, thin, tall, and yellowing maize plants with tiny or no cobs, some bending over.
